example: Example run with fictional figures: Northbrook Trading, AP accruals at 30 September 2026. The figures match the worked examples on the step-by-step page.

chosen.warehouse-log-september.xlsx: the name of the user's own receipt log

messages.text: What AP do we need to accrue for September?
I can work that out. Before I read anything, I need seven answers. I ask them all at once, so the run does not stop again for each one.
list: Do you want me to use MosoFin, or will you upload the data?
Which period, with exact dates? And do you keep the books on the accrual basis or the cash basis?
Where do you log goods receipts? Do you have service confirmations or time sheets?
How many days after month end do I search for late bills? I propose the day that the books close.
Can you recover input tax, and in which country?
Which materiality threshold applies to accruals? Is it tighter at year end?

messages.text: Use MosoFin. 1 to 30 September, accrual basis. The warehouse logs every delivery in a sheet, attached. We close on 10 October. Use Accrued Expenses. We recover no input tax. Materiality is $500 all year.

messages.label: Checked the workspace and what your books hold
messages.summary: The agent can read your books. It cannot change them.

messages.text: Here is my plan. I build the **September** AP accrual schedule for **Northbrook Trading**, on the accrual basis. Orders, bills and supplier history come from MosoFin. Receipts come from your warehouse log. I search for late bills from **1 to 10 October**. Accruals go to **Accrued Expenses**, with no input-tax line. Materiality is **$500**.
messages.after: No tool can see your inbox. Please send me each bill that came in after 30 September and is not in the books yet. Then shall I start?

messages.text: Two came in. Yes, go ahead.

messages.label: Read the books in one batch
rows: Open from 14 Jul: PO-2033, PO-2041, PO-2044
Includes RW-8812, with no order number
Includes Summit Cleaning and Crestline Logistics
messages.summary: 8 reads in one batch, and your log. Nothing in your books changed.

messages.text: Your supplier history shows suppliers that bill each month. Please confirm this list, and add any supplier that the books do not show:
messages.after: Crestline billed $1,000 in each of June, July and August. Its contract letter says $1,500. Which amount do I use?

messages.text: The list is right, but take out Power Co. Our other accruals run already has the electricity. Crestline's new contract is right.
First, the goods. Your log shows what arrived, and the orders give the price:

card.title: Goods received, not invoiced
rows: + PO-2033 line 1, received and billed on RW-8812

messages.after: RW-8812 has no order number. I matched it by supplier, date, amount and description, and I mark the match as **inferred**. The other **$4,200** of open orders did not arrive, so I do not accrue it.

messages.text: Next, the late bills. The service period decides the month, not the bill date:
messages.after: PD-305 for $2,400 goes to Exceptions. If that work was all in September, September misses up to $2,400. HOS-4410 for $640 is dated 30 September. Please enter it as a September bill. I do not accrue it.

messages.text: Then the regular suppliers. Two go in, and two are below your threshold:
messages.after: Metro Shred at $120 and Keystone at $350 are each below $500. I list them with their total of **$470**. Lakeside and Power Co each appear once, in another place.

messages.text: I propose these accruals. Each one credits Accrued Expenses and reverses on Thursday 1 October:
messages.after: Stock rises by **$6,600** and September cost rises by **$8,050**. Accrued Expenses opened at $1,950, and both August reversals posted. So it closes at **$14,650**.

messages.text: To be safe, can you also accrue all the open purchase orders?
No. PO-2044 and 60 units on PO-2033 never arrived. That **$4,200** is an order, not a debt. I list it only as open orders, not received.
messages.after: Five items go to Exceptions, each with an owner and a due date of Friday 9 October. A person posts the entries. I do not. Do you want the seven sheets as an Excel file? And shall I save your settings for next month?

messages.text: Done. The Excel file has the seven sheets. I saved your answers, the regular suppliers with their expected amounts, the accounts and your warehouse log as the receipt record. Power Co stays out next month too.
